sections.h2: Selling a Rochester house: what to know first
sections.html:
Rochester, the Olmsted County seat, lies in the bluff country of southeast Minnesota, 85 miles from the Twin Cities. It had 124,292 residents on July 1, 2025, 2.4 percent more than in April 2020, and only two Minnesota cities are bigger. Medicine drives the economy, and workers and students keep a steady stream of renters and first-time buyers in the market.

Not every owner has time for a retail listing. Typical situations in a university and hospital town include:

  • a relocation after a residency, fellowship or job change;
  • a rental left behind by a tenant who moved out;
  • a house inherited from a relative who lived far away;
  • an older home with deferred repairs that would be expensive to fix before listing.

sections.h2: Older houses, wind and storm damage
sections.html:
Rochester gets around 33 inches of rain and nearly 52 inches of snow in a typical year, and the January to April stretch is the windiest. Severe storms have left a record, including tornadoes in 1953, 1962 and June 2010 and a June 2019 storm in southwest Rochester.

  • Roof and siding that have taken years of wind are the first things an inspector looks at.
  • Basements near the Zumbro and its creeks deserve a moisture check before you list or accept an offer.
  • Frozen-pipe damage in a vacant house is a real winter risk, so keep the heat on during a sale.

Cash buyers commonly accept a storm-worn house as is, so you skip the repair bids.

Construction near the river and the medical campus can change the feel of a nearby block, and buyers near downtown will likely raise it. Rochester Public Schools divides the city into John Marshall, Mayo and Century high school zones, so ask the district which zone an address falls in before it goes into a listing.

Anyone renting out a dwelling in Rochester needs a Rental Housing Certificate under city ordinance chapter 7-3-2, including a single-family house the owner does not live in. Renting without one is a misdemeanor punishable by up to a $1,000 fine, 90 days in jail, or both.

  • Certificates renew each year, and the fee depends on the number of units.
  • Inspection scores set a one, two, three or four year cycle, and a compliant inspection is required in the year it is due.
  • A certificate must be transferred within 30 days of a property sale, and the city has a termination form for owners who have sold.
  • A building that sits vacant must be registered within 30 days under ordinance 7-14-6, and an annual vacant building fee follows.

Short stays of up to 30 days follow separate rules. A second home listed on a rental platform needs a Short Term Rental license and a compliant inspection, while an owner-occupied room rental needs registration. For questions, the Community Development office is at 4001 W. River Parkway NW, Suite 100, and the city's main line is 507-328-2311.

sections.h2: Olmsted County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
House tax is split into a May 15 payment and an October 15 payment, while farm parcels run later, in mid-November. The next bill for a house comes due in May.

For a sale during the year, the county prorates tax at closing. The seller owes tax from January until closing day, and the buyer owes it from closing through December 31. A seller who prepaid the entire year is repaid for the buyer's part. A buyer who closes mid-year receives no mailed statement, yet late payment is still late.

After a sale the county mails the new owner a homestead application. Return it, because the homestead classification determines the value exclusion that lowers the tax bill. Questions go to the county's revenue and records line at 507-328-7636.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Rochester property value
sections.html:
Gather recent appraisals or comparable sales and bring them to the Assessor's Office (507-328-7670, Property Records, 151 4th Street SE). Unresolved disputes go to the meetings printed on the valuation notice, local board first where one exists and the county board where it does not.

Past that, the Minnesota Tax Court takes petitions once the valuation notice has arrived, with an April 30 cutoff in the year the tax is payable. A petition can be served by email or delivered in person to the County Attorney's Office on Fourth Street Southeast. Valuation notices arrive each spring, which opens a fresh round every year.

sections.h2: A step-by-step order for a quick Rochester sale
sections.html: Decide first whether the house is a rental, because that sets the city paperwork. If it is, check the certificate and the inspection cycle, then ask Community Development how the transfer will work. Next, test for radon or gather the results you already have, and write down what you know about the house. Collect cash offers, compare the check amount and closing date, and sign with the buyer you trust. The deed then goes to the recorder with the deed tax, and the year's property tax is prorated between you and the buyer. Hold on to your latest tax statement for the title company. Ask the buyer in writing when you must move out.

The state deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration, with a flat $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less (Minn. Stat. 287.21), and the recorder collects it as soon as the deed arrives. Ask Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing how it wants deeds submitted.

State law adds a radon step ahead of any signed sale agreement: the seller discloses test results and any mitigation system in writing and hands over the Department of Health booklet on radon in real estate (Minn. Stat. 144.496). Transfers to heirs are exempt.

Before you sign anything, also gather what you know about the house for the written disclosure of material facts, and settle any rental certificate questions so the closing is not delayed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rochester house without fixing it first?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer takes it as is. Material facts you know about still go to the buyer in writing (Minn. Stat. 513.55), and a landlord should settle the rental certificate and inspection status before taking an offer on an occupied rental.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell a buyer about radon?
faqs.a: Yes. Minnesota requires a written radon disclosure before you sign an agreement to sell residential property, and a seller who withholds known radon facts can be sued within two years after closing. The disclosure covers any tests, reports and mitigation system you know about.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental certificate when I sell a Rochester rental?
faqs.a: It has to be transferred within 30 days of the sale, and the city offers a termination form for owners who have sold. Contact Community Development at 507-328-2311 so the certificate does not stay in your name.

faqs.q: How is tax split when a Rochester house closes?
faqs.a: Tax from January up to closing is the seller's, and tax from closing through December 31 is the buyer's. A seller who prepaid the full year is reimbursed at closing for the buyer's share.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Rochester assessment?
faqs.a: Each spring, once the valuation notice arrives. Start with the county meetings, and file any Minnesota Tax Court petition by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.
